mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) when FEDFUNDS declines over the prior 30 days, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% over three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) when UNRATE exceeds 4.0% for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals broad demand weakness, triggering a sell-off in equities; the interaction of these two series is the key driver of negative returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) when both RSAFS and HOUST decline by more than 1% in the prior month, or the interaction term in a regression has p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), a decline in industrial production signals an imminent economic slowdown, prompting market anticipation of a policy pivot and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% in the prior month and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production over the past month signals a supply contraction, leading to higher inflation and real interest rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% in the prior month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the consumer price index above 5.0% year-over-year signals persistent inflation, leading to a hawkish monetary policy response and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) when CPIAUCSL exceeds 5.0% YoY, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market contraction (e.g., falling labor force participation), triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days; the interaction of these series is critical.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) when PAYEMS declines by more than 0.5% and UNRATE declines by more than 0.2pp in the prior month, or the interaction term in a regression has p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 (index base 2017=100) signals a significant manufacturing slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) when INDPRO falls below 100, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
